task: A rod 10 mm in diameter (Young's modulus 200 GPa) stretches by 0.5 mm under a 10 kN tensile load. Find its length, then model the rod as a solid cylinder of that diameter and length.
A rod 8 mm in diameter (Young's modulus 70 GPa) stretches by 0.3 mm under a 5 kN tensile load. Find its length, then model the rod as a solid cylinder of that diameter and length.
A rod 12 mm in diameter (Young's modulus 110 GPa) stretches by 1 mm under a 20 kN tensile load. Find its length, then model the rod as a solid cylinder of that diameter and length.
A car braking from 20 m/s decelerates at 8 m/s^2. Find its stopping distance, then model a 1:100 scale test strip as a plate that long (the scaled length), 50 mm wide and 3 mm thick.
A car braking from 15 m/s decelerates at 5 m/s^2. Find its stopping distance, then model a 1:100 scale test strip as a plate that long (the scaled length), 50 mm wide and 3 mm thick.
A car braking from 30 m/s decelerates at 6 m/s^2. Find its stopping distance, then model a 1:100 scale test strip as a plate that long (the scaled length), 50 mm wide and 3 mm thick.

A heater runs at 1000 W from a 230 V supply and is made of wire 0.5 mm in diameter with resistivity 1.1e-06 ohm m. Find the wire length, then model a straight 2 mm diameter rod with that length as a stand-in for the wire.

A heater runs at 600 W from a 120 V supply and is made of wire 0.4 mm in diameter with resistivity 1.1e-06 ohm m. Find the wire length, then model a straight 2 mm diameter rod with that length as a stand-in for the wire.

A heater runs at 50 W from a 24 V supply and is made of wire 0.3 mm in diameter with resistivity 4.9e-07 ohm m. Find the wire length, then model a straight 2 mm diameter rod with that length as a stand-in for the wire.

A square cooling fin must shed 20 W by convection with a heat transfer coefficient of 25 W/(m^2 K) and a 40 K temperature difference (count one face only). Find the side of the square, then model the fin as a square plate with that side, 2 mm thick.

A square cooling fin must shed 50 W by convection with a heat transfer coefficient of 10 W/(m^2 K) and a 60 K temperature difference (count one face only). Find the side of the square, then model the fin as a square plate with that side, 2 mm thick.

A square cooling fin must shed 5 W by convection with a heat transfer coefficient of 15 W/(m^2 K) and a 25 K temperature difference (count one face only). Find the side of the square, then model the fin as a square plate with that side, 2 mm thick.
Water must flow at 2 L/s through a pipe at a mean speed of 1.5 m/s. Find the pipe's inside diameter, then model 200 mm of the pipe as a tube with that inside diameter and a 5 mm wall.
Water must flow at 0.5 L/s through a pipe at a mean speed of 1 m/s. Find the pipe's inside diameter, then model 200 mm of the pipe as a tube with that inside diameter and a 5 mm wall.
Water must flow at 10 L/s through a pipe at a mean speed of 2.5 m/s. Find the pipe's inside diameter, then model 200 mm of the pipe as a tube with that inside diameter and a 5 mm wall.

A thin-walled cylindrical pressure vessel with a 200 mm inside diameter holds 2 MPa, and the hoop stress may not exceed 100 MPa. Find the minimum wall thickness, then model a 100 mm long section of the vessel as a tube with that inside diameter and wall thickness.

A thin-walled cylindrical pressure vessel with a 120 mm inside diameter holds 5 MPa, and the hoop stress may not exceed 150 MPa. Find the minimum wall thickness, then model a 100 mm long section of the vessel as a tube with that inside diameter and wall thickness.

A thin-walled cylindrical pressure vessel with a 400 mm inside diameter holds 1 MPa, and the hoop stress may not exceed 80 MPa. Find the minimum wall thickness, then model a 100 mm long section of the vessel as a tube with that inside diameter and wall thickness.
An object moves in a circle at 10 m/s with a centripetal acceleration of 50 m/s^2. Find the radius, then model a 1:10 scale turntable as a disc 8 mm thick with that scaled radius.
An object moves in a circle at 6 m/s with a centripetal acceleration of 30 m/s^2. Find the radius, then model a 1:10 scale turntable as a disc 8 mm thick with that scaled radius.
An object moves in a circle at 15 m/s with a centripetal acceleration of 100 m/s^2. Find the radius, then model a 1:10 scale turntable as a disc 8 mm thick with that scaled radius.
A rocket nozzle exhausts 2 kg/s of gas of density 0.5 kg/m^3 at 2000 m/s. Find the exit diameter, then model a cover plate as a disc of that diameter, 4 mm thick, with a 6 mm hole at its center.
A rocket nozzle exhausts 0.5 kg/s of gas of density 0.8 kg/m^3 at 1500 m/s. Find the exit diameter, then model a cover plate as a disc of that diameter, 4 mm thick, with a 6 mm hole at its center.
A rocket nozzle exhausts 5 kg/s of gas of density 0.3 kg/m^3 at 2500 m/s. Find the exit diameter, then model a cover plate as a disc of that diameter, 4 mm thick, with a 6 mm hole at its center.

A wing has an area of 12.5 m^2 and an aspect ratio of 8. Find its span, then model a 1:20 scale model of the wing as a flat plate as long as the scaled span, as wide as the scaled mean chord (area / span, scaled), and 10 mm thick.

A wing has an area of 6 m^2 and an aspect ratio of 6. Find its span, then model a 1:20 scale model of the wing as a flat plate as long as the scaled span, as wide as the scaled mean chord (area / span, scaled), and 10 mm thick.

A wing has an area of 16.9 m^2 and an aspect ratio of 10. Find its span, then model a 1:20 scale model of the wing as a flat plate as long as the scaled span, as wide as the scaled mean chord (area / span, scaled), and 10 mm thick.

A resistor made of nichrome wire (resistivity 1.1e-6 ohm m), 0.5 mm in diameter, must draw 2 A from 12 V. Find the wire length, then model a straight rod of that length, 3 mm in diameter, as a stand-in.

A resistor made of nichrome wire (resistivity 1.1e-6 ohm m), 0.25 mm in diameter, must draw 0.5 A from 5 V. Find the wire length, then model a straight rod of that length, 3 mm in diameter, as a stand-in.

A resistor made of nichrome wire (resistivity 1.1e-6 ohm m), 0.8 mm in diameter, must draw 3 A from 24 V. Find the wire length, then model a straight rod of that length, 3 mm in diameter, as a stand-in.

A parallel-plate capacitor has square plates 50 mm on a side and a dielectric of relative permittivity 4, and must have a capacitance of 100 pF (vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m). Find the plate gap, then model the dielectric spacer as a square plate 50 mm on a side with that thickness.

A parallel-plate capacitor has square plates 100 mm on a side and a dielectric of relative permittivity 3, and must have a capacitance of 1000 pF (vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m). Find the plate gap, then model the dielectric spacer as a square plate 100 mm on a side with that thickness.

A parallel-plate capacitor has square plates 30 mm on a side and a dielectric of relative permittivity 2.5, and must have a capacitance of 47 pF (vacuum permittivity 8.854e-12 F/m). Find the plate gap, then model the dielectric spacer as a square plate 30 mm on a side with that thickness.
A ball is launched at 20 m/s at 45 degrees over level ground (g = 9.81 m/s^2). Find its range, then model a 1:100 scale rail as a bar as long as the scaled range, 10 mm wide and 10 mm tall.
A ball is launched at 35 m/s at 45 degrees over level ground (g = 9.81 m/s^2). Find its range, then model a 1:100 scale rail as a bar as long as the scaled range, 10 mm wide and 10 mm tall.
A ball is launched at 12 m/s at 45 degrees over level ground (g = 9.81 m/s^2). Find its range, then model a 1:100 scale rail as a bar as long as the scaled range, 10 mm wide and 10 mm tall.

A cylindrical float 150 mm in diameter carries 3 kg in fresh water (1000 kg/m^3), ignoring its own weight. Find how deep it sinks, then model the submerged part as a solid cylinder of that diameter and depth.

A cylindrical float 80 mm in diameter carries 0.8 kg in fresh water (1000 kg/m^3), ignoring its own weight. Find how deep it sinks, then model the submerged part as a solid cylinder of that diameter and depth.

A cylindrical float 300 mm in diameter carries 10 kg in fresh water (1000 kg/m^3), ignoring its own weight. Find how deep it sinks, then model the submerged part as a solid cylinder of that diameter and depth.
A copper strip (resistivity 1.68e-8 ohm m) 500 mm long and 3 mm thick must have a resistance of 0.2 milliohm. Find its width, then model the strip, 500 mm long, that wide and 3 mm thick.
